champion: Scleroderma-like illness due to meperidine injections
ordered_diagnoses: Scleroderma-like illness due to meperidine injections
Contracture of the deltoid, triceps, and biceps muscles

facts.raw_span: 7-year history of severe, mechanical, low back pain
long-standing mental depression
self-administering subcutaneous injections of meperidine, 100 mg 4 times per day, for the past 3 years
Large and deep, irregularly shaped, cutaneous ulcer on the dorsum of right forearm with necrotic tissue and muscle exposure at the base
Woody induration of skin on both forearms and abdominal region
Bilateral contracture of deltoid, triceps, and biceps muscles
Active and passive range of motion restricted at shoulders and elbows
No signs of joint inflammation
Elevated serum creatinine kinase (192 U/L; reference range, 0-174 U/L)
Normal complete blood cell count
Shows lobular panniculitis, subcutaneous fat lobules with necrotic adipocytes and dense inflammatory infiltrates composed mainly of foamy histiocytes
Deltoid muscle biopsy showed no muscle involvement

concepts.preferred_label: Scleroderma-like illness due to meperidine injections
concepts.why: The patient's history of self-administering subcutaneous injections of meperidine, combined with the presence of large and deep cutaneous ulcers, woody induration of skin, and histopathological findings of lobular panniculitis, suggests a scleroderma-like illness due to meperidine injections.

concepts.preferred_label: Contracture of the deltoid, triceps, and biceps muscles
concepts.why: The patient's bilateral contracture of deltoid, triceps, and biceps muscles, along with restricted range of motion at shoulders and elbows, suggests a diagnosis of contracture of these muscles.

The patient's histopathological findings of lobular panniculitis, subcutaneous fat lobules with necrotic adipocytes, and dense inflammatory infiltrates composed mainly of foamy histiocytes, support a diagnosis of panniculitis.

The patient's history of self-administering subcutaneous injections of meperidine, combined with the presence of woody induration of skin and histopathological findings of severe fibrosis, suggests a diagnosis of meperidine-induced fibrosis.

The patient's elevated serum creatinine kinase levels, combined with the presence of bilateral contracture of deltoid, triceps, and biceps muscles, and restricted range of motion at shoulders and elbows, suggests a diagnosis of muscle fibrosis.

rationales.F03: Meperidine injections are a known cause of scleroderma-like illness and fibrosis.
rationales.F04: The presence of a large and deep cutaneous ulcer is consistent with panniculitis and meperidine-induced fibrosis.
rationales.F05: Woody induration of the skin is a characteristic feature of scleroderma-like illness due to meperidine injections.
rationales.F06: Bilateral contracture of the deltoid, triceps, and biceps muscles is consistent with meperidine-induced fibrosis and muscle fibrosis.
rationales.F09: Elevated serum creatinine kinase levels suggest muscle damage, which is consistent with meperidine-induced fibrosis and muscle fibrosis.
rationales.F11: The histopathological findings of lobular panniculitis and dense inflammatory infiltrates are consistent with panniculitis and meperidine-induced fibrosis.
rationales.F12: The absence of muscle involvement in the deltoid muscle biopsy rules out muscle fibrosis as a primary diagnosis.
